{{Quote|Destiny has but one throne, and if the Jedi queen claims it, the Sith cannot.|[[Sarasu Taalon]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], after seeing Allana seated on the [[Throne of Balance]]|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref>}}
In [[44 ABY]], [[Sith Saber]] [[Gavar Khai]] developed the '''Jedi Queen project''', which involved the [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] of [[Hapan]] [[Queen Mother]] [[Tenel Ka Djo]] in order to prevent the birth of an influential [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Queen/Legends|queen]] of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] descent. Charged with the [[Lost Tribe of Sith emergence|mission]], Saber [[Querdan Dei]] pursued the Hapan queen to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]], but was ultimately [[Death/Legends|slain]] in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] with [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]].

==Prelude==
In [[44 ABY]], [[High Lord (Circle of Lords)|High Lord]] [[Sarasu Taalon]] of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] experienced a [[Throne of Balance|vision]] of a young [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Queen/Legends|queen]], one who ruled [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in the name of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]. Taalon became obsessed with the prevention of a galactic throne upon which sat a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] sovereign, but he was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in [[Battle in the Fallanassi village|battle]] before his plan could come to fruition. [[Sith Saber]] [[Gavar Khai]], who had frequently served with Taalon during the [[Sith/Legends|Sith's]] recent [[Lost Tribe of Sith emergence|battles]] with the Jedi, became equally determined to act in his late [[Commander/Legends|commander's]] stead. He labeled the mission the Jedi Queen project, and the Sith ultimately discovered that [[Hapan]] [[Queen Mother]] [[Tenel Ka Djo]]'s appearance was similar to that of the future Jedi queen's, and they feared that Djo would give birth to the queen. Unbeknownst to the Sith, she already had a daughter&mdash;[[Allana Djo Solo|Allana Solo]], disguised as "Amelia," the adopted daughter of [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]]. Hoping to prevent a future that had in reality already come to be, Khai charged Sith Saber [[Querdan Dei]] with the [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] of Djo.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Jedi Queen project==
[[File:Allana_Solo_by_Brian_Rood.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Allana Solo, the target]]
Aboard an [[EE-104 Fisheye|EE-104 ''Fisheye'']] called ''[[Cryptic Warning]]'', Dei and his crew&mdash;[[Hara]], [[Sazat]], and Dei's son, [[Fardan Dei|Fardan]]&mdash;ventured to the [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]], with instructions to gain access to and [[Death/Legends|kill]] the Queen Mother. The Sith detected a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Hapan Battle Dragon]]s heading for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]] with Tenel Ka Djo on board. Querdan Dei and his crew followed the [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] to Klatooine, where they also found that the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] had landed. Observation of the camp on Klatooine revealed that it was an unofficial [[Mission to Klatooine|mission]] for negotiations after the planet's recent [[Liberation|uprising]] against their former [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] masters. Dei performed some reconnaissance around the camp and formulated a plan to carry out his mission.<ref name="Conviction" />

Dei captured one of the [[Solo family/Legends|Solo family's]] [[Droid/Legends|droids]], [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], and planted a bomb inside of him. Dei then paid a [[2-1B surgical droid/Legends|2-1B surgical droid]] that was part of a droid's rights group to take C-3PO and pretend that it had captured the Solos' droid. The Solos' supposedly adopted daughter, Amelia, found the droid and rescued it from the droid's rights group, then took it with her to assist Djo with translation. Dei planned to activate the droid once it was close enough to Djo, but as he waited, he determined that Amelia could in fact be Djo's daughter, as she was very similar in appearance. Dei resolved to kill Amelia as well, and when C-3PO was in position, he reached for his controller to activate the bomb in the droid. However, Amelia had sneaked up behind him and taken the remote. Dei demanded that she give it back, and although she refused, he was able to determine that Djo was indeed Amelia's mother.<ref name="Conviction" />

The Sith Saber charged the young Amelia with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], but before he could harm her he was intercepted by the girl's pet [[Nexu/Legends|nexu]], [[Anji]]. Anji ripped out his [[Eye/Legends|eye]] before he was able to throw the nexu off of him, and as he prepared to renew his attack on Amelia, he found himself face-to-face instead with Leia Solo. She requested Dei's surrender, but he refused, and they engaged in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. The duel lasted for several minutes, but eventually Dei spun in such a way that he lost sight of Solo due to his newly-lost eye, and she killed him.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Aftermath==
Soon afterward, a larger Sith force under the command of Gavar Khai failed in their [[Operation Shieldfall|mission]] to capture the powerful [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] entity [[Abeloth]] on the planet [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios]]. Abeloth contacted Khai after the battle to form an alliance against their mutual enemy, the Jedi. Khai agreed,<ref name="Conviction" /> although Abeloth soon afterward betrayed the Sith and [[Destruction of Tahv|destroyed]] their [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]], [[Tahv]]. Khai fell under Abeloth's influence, however, and left the Sith, joining the entity's [[Abeloth's fleet|forces]] instead. Although Khai still showed interest in preventing the Jedi queen from coming to be, Abeloth refused to allow him to continue the Jedi Queen project.<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The groundwork for the Jedi Queen project was initially laid down in author [[Troy Denning]]'s ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]'', the sixth novel in the nine-part [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series, wherein Taalon had his vision of the Jedi queen and was later killed. The project was first named and carried out in [[Aaron Allston]]'s ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'', the seventh novel of the series. The project was only mentioned in the eighth novel, [[Christie Golden]]'s ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]'', wherein it was officially cancelled by Abeloth.
